In the previous application exercise, we used a linear regression model with one predictor to study body mass of penguins from the Palmer archipelago.
In this exercise, we will use *both* a numerical predictor and a categorical predictor to model body mass.
We will also investigate whether the relationship between flipper length and body mass might differ by island.


## Getting started

### Packages

We will use the **tidyverse** package for data visualization and wrangling, the **tidymodels** package for modeling, and the **palmerpenguins** package for the data.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(palmerpenguins)
```


## The main-effects model

So far, we fit the following **main effects** model:

```{r}
#| label: fit-main-effects-model

bm_fl_island_main <- linear_reg() |>
  fit(
    body_mass_g ~ flipper_length_mm + island,
    data = penguins
    )

tidy(bm_fl_island_main)
```

- In this model, what assumption do we make about the relationship between flipper length and body mass across the three islands?

*Add your response here.*

## Could the slopes differ?

The following plot also fits a separate regression line for each island.

```{r}
#| label: visualize-separate-lines
#| message: false
#| warning: false
ggplot(
  penguins,
  aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = island)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(end = 0.85) +
  labs(
    x = "Flipper length (mm)",
    y = "Body mass (g)",
    color = "Island",
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

- How do these lines differ from the parallel fitted lines produced by the main effects model?

*Add your response here.*

## Fitting an interaction model

An **interaction effects** model allows the slope for flipper length to differ across islands.
In a model formula, `island * flipper_length_mm` includes:

- the main effect of `island`,
- the main effect of `flipper_length_mm`, and
- their interaction.

## Comparing the two models visually

- Set the following code cell's `eval` option to `true` to render the visualizations of main and interaction effect models. Describe what the code is doing.

```{r}
#| label: compare-model-plots
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

bm_fl_island_main_aug <- augment(
  bm_fl_island_main,
  new_data = penguins
)

ggplot(
  bm_fl_island_main_aug,
  aes(x = flipper_length_mm, color = island)
) +
  geom_point(aes(y = body_mass_g), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = .pred), linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(end = 0.85) +
  labs(
    x = "Flipper length (mm)",
    y = "Body mass (g)",
    color = "island",
    title = "Main-effects model"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")


bm_fl_island_int_aug <- augment(
  bm_fl_island_int,
  new_data = penguins
)

ggplot(
  bm_fl_island_int_aug,
  aes(x = flipper_length_mm, color = island)
) +
  geom_point(aes(y = body_mass_g), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = .pred), linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(end = 0.85) +
  labs(
    x = "Flipper length (mm)",
    y = "Body mass (g)",
    color = "island",
    title = "Interaction model"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
